pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Barium Toxicity (Barium Carbonate Ingestion) THE SMOKING GUN: Profound, treatment-refractory hypokalemia paired with ascending flaccid paralysis and marked hypertension after ingesting an unlabeled white powder (barium carbonate rodenticide/ceramic flux). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Absorbed barium ions (Ba2+) act as potent, non-selective blockers of inwardly rectifying potassium (Kir) channels across skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle membranes. By preventing passive potassium efflux, barium traps potassium intracellularly, causing dramatic extracellular hypokalemia. This severe transmembrane ionic disturbance depolarizes resting cell membrane potentials, producing diffuse muscle paralysis, respiratory collapse, severe vascular constriction (hypertension), and life-threatening ventricular dysrhythmias. Intravenous sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate is administered as an antidote to precipitate soluble barium into non-absorbable barium sulfate, alongside aggressive potassium replacement and hemodialysis.
